schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE `atom` (
  `atom_id` TEXT NOT NULL,
  `molecule_id` TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  `element` TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`atom_id`),
  FOREIGN KEY (`molecule_id`) REFERENCES `molecule` (`molecule_id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `bond` (
  `bond_id` TEXT NOT NULL,
  `molecule_id` TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  `bond_type` TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`bond_id`),
  FOREIGN KEY (`molecule_id`) REFERENCES `molecule` (`molecule_id`)
);

CREATE TABLE `connected` (
  `atom_id` TEXT NOT NULL,
  `atom_id2` TEXT NOT NULL,
  `bond_id` TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`atom_id`,`atom_id2`),
  FOREIGN KEY (`atom_id`) REFERENCES `atom` (`atom_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  FOREIGN KEY (`atom_id2`) REFERENCES `atom` (`atom_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  FOREIGN KEY (`bond_id`) REFERENCES `bond` (`bond_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
);

CREATE TABLE `molecule` (
  `molecule_id` TEXT NOT NULL,
  `label` TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`molecule_id`)
);
q1: SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN T.label = '+' THEN T.molecule_id ELSE NULL END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(T.molecule_id) FROM molecule AS t
q2: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN label = '+' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(molecule_id) FROM molecule

explanation: Both queries are calculating the percentage of molecules with a label of '+' out of the total number of molecules. The difference in the implementation is that Q1 uses COUNT(CASE WHEN T.label = '+' THEN T.molecule_id ELSE NULL END) to count the number of molecules with a label of '+', while Q2 uses SUM(CASE WHEN label = '+' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) to achieve the same result. Both methods are semantically equivalent as they both count the number of molecules with a label of '+' and divide it by the total number of molecules, then multiply by 100 to get the percentage.
